Smithsonian naturalists also note that the richest areas for water fowl are in Western Panama on the Atlantic side. These provide stopover alternatives for migrants so that loss of these Canal Zone sites would not be critical or disagrous for these species. With regard to migrating land birds, whose numbers appear to be decreasing, less is known and areas such as the Pipeline Road could be important for their survival.
1. Panamanian Development Plans
The Panamanian Government has three development projects planned for areas in the Canal Zone after the Treaty comes into force.
-- A new highway is projected from the west end of the Balboa-Rodman bridge following the shoreline through Fort Kobbe-Howard Air Force Base to Vera Cruz. Since it will pass through military areas, the U.S. will have to approve its route and design. It will skirt the Farfan Marsh and there may be some archeological sites along the route. These interests will have to be protected before the road will be approved.
-- A new container port is planned for the Coco Solo naval base area. Other areas for possible construction of the port were examined but rejected because of the adverse ecological impact involved. The naval base has been an operating port facility for 40 years, is located in an existing urban area, and will involve no new construction. Consequently there should be no significant adverse environmental effects. (See map at Tab K.)
